source.title: CPSample: Classifier Protected Sampling for Guarding Training Data During Diffusion
source.authors: Joshua Kazdan; Hao Sun; Jia-Qi Han; Felix Petersen; Frederick Vu; Stefano Ermon

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains classifiers on random labels and reports their cross-entropy, testing random-label fitting in a diffusion-classifier setting. It does not reproduce the original study's full train/test-error comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper reports classifier cross-entropy below 0.05 for experiments in Sections 4.1 and 4.2. This is an aggregate result; it does not report classifier test error or a comparison with training on true labels. Other reported results concern diffusion sampling and privacy, not the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Although random-label memorization is used as a tool for diffusion privacy protection, Section 3.2 reports the classifiers' own fitting loss below 0.05. This directly bears on V1 in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: CPSample uses a classifier trained to memorize random binary labels to steer diffusion sampling away from training images, and the authors report classifier cross-entropy below 0.05 for Sections 4.1 and 4.2.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains modified U-Net classifiers on noisy images with random binary labels to guide diffusion sampling; it does not reproduce the original network training and generalization comparison.
record.problems: The random-label classifier result is reported only as an aggregate cross-entropy statement. The paper does not report classifier test error, a true-label comparison, or separate random-label fitting results by dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No other paper results meet the row criteria for these claim versions. Classifier training-step counts and diffusion privacy, similarity, membership-inference, and FID results do not measure the other listed versions.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Training-time comparison with true labels and convergence as label corruption increases. Classifier training durations alone do not test these comparisons.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or entirely Gaussian-noise inputs. Noise-corrupted images retaining their original image identity do not establish these results.
Training and test error across increasing fractions of corrupted labels.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noise, including comparisons over training.

record.verdict_notes: Intentional random-label training is the intervention specified by V1, so it does not itself disqualify the fitting result. The authors describe difficulty scaling classifier training, but provide no corresponding fitting failure rates or true-label controls.

versions.untested_parts: Test error at chance, comparison with training on true labels, and whether fitting required no changes to architecture or training hyperparameters.

rows.subject: classifier models in Sections 4.1 and 4.2 (aggregate; individual classifiers not reported separately)
rows.operation_detail: Trained a classifier on random binary labels assigned to training images, using noise-corrupted images and timestep as inputs.
rows.note: Aggregate statement across experiments in Sections 4.1 and 4.2; the text does not provide separate losses for datasets or classifiers. Appendix C says classifiers were modified U-Nets trained from scratch on subsets, including 1000-image subsets, but does not associate separate results with each classifier.
rows.check: The aggregate cross-entropy value is correctly extracted and supports strong random-label fitting. It is not a measured classification-error rate and does not establish zero error for every image or noise timestep.
